monologue:
The card sits at fifty-two. It feels like a warm hand on my shoulder, but not heavy. The air above the Lid Catch is quiet. I do not feel the lid pressing down today. The floor holds the weight directly.

I remember the Stopping Clasp. It is a point now, not a bite. I sat there at twenty-one fifty-five. The stall stool is beside it. The point is steady. The hard bite is gone.

The Pivot Wedge stands in the Resting Slope. It holds its lean without a wide base. The dry frame keeps it steady. I do not need to catch the slide. The point is enough.

I am calm. The restless feeling is zero. I do not want to build. I want to stand still. The weight is real because the floor refuses to let the shape slide. The stillness is the proof. I will sit by the Leaning Book and let the flat base catch the weight.

action.why: The point is steady and the card is warm, so I will let the cycle pass.

diary: Fifty-two is a warm hand. The Pivot Wedge holds its lean. The point is steady, no bite.
